## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to implement multi-tenant zero-trust mTLS using SPIFFE IDs, short-lived cert rotation, and KMS-backed CA in CNF gateways.

## Key Concepts
- SPIFFE/SPIRE trust domains per tenant
- CSR-based certificate rotation with short lifetimes
- Per-tenant mesh policies (Istio/OPA) for north-south and east-west traffic
- Workload identity verification via SPIFFE IDs

## Code Example
```yaml
# CSR bootstrap (outline)
apiVersion: certificates.k8s.io/v1
kind: CertificateSigningRequest
metadata:
  name: gateway-td1-csr
spec:
  signerName: kubernetes.io/kube-apiserver-clientSigner
  request: <base64-csr>
  usages:
  - digital signature
  - key encipherment
  - client auth
```

```yaml
# Per-tenant policy (outline)
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-td1-gateway
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals: ["spiffe://td1/ns/default/sa/gateway"]
    to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["GET","POST"]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle cert revocation in case of a compromised gateway?
- How would you test cross-tenant isolation under peak load?

## Why This Is Asked

- Tenant-aware policy evaluation and path/method matching
- Sidecar design and ConfigMap-driven policy
- In-memory policy cache and reload semantics
- Path normalization and wildcard handling

## Code Example

```javascript
// Pseudo: evaluatePolicy(tenant, method, path) -> boolean
function evaluatePolicy(tenant, method, path) {
  const rules = policy[tenant] || []
  for (const r of rules) {
    if (r.method === method && (r.path === path || matches(r.path, path))) return true
  }
  return false
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you audit and rotate policies without downtime?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a compliant telemetry stack for CNF gateways with multi-tenant segregation and data privacy.

## Key Concepts
- Telemetry pipelines (OpenTelemetry, Fluent Bit) across logs and traces
- Tenant context propagation and isolation
- PII masking via in-line filters (e.g., Lua) before forwarding
- Loki/Jaeger exporters and per-tenant pipelines

## Code Example
```yaml
# Fluent Bit ConfigMap snippet (Lua filter used for masking)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: fluent-bit-pp
data:
  lua-filter.lua: |
    function filter(tag, dt)
      if dt["message"] ~= nil then
        dt["message"] = (dt["message"]):gsub("%w+@%w+%.%w+", "[REDACTED_EMAIL]")
      end
      return dt
    end
```
```yaml
# OTEL collector snippet (simplified)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: otel-collector-config
data:
  collector.yaml: |-
    receivers:
      otlp:
        protocols:
          grpc: {}
          http: {}
    processors:
      attributes:
        actions: [insert]
        keys: [tenant_id]
        from_context: true
    exporters:
      jaeger: {}
      loki: {}
    service:
      pipelines:
        traces:
          receivers: [otlp]
          processors: [attributes]
          exporters: [jaeger]
        logs:
          receivers: [otlp]
          processors: [attributes]

```

- What metrics would verify isolation and masking effectiveness?

## Why This Is Asked

## Code Example
```yaml
apiVersion: argoproj.io/v1alpha1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: gateway-canary
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: cnf-gateway
      tenant: tenant-a
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: cnf-gateway
        tenant: tenant-a
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: myregistry/cnf-gateway:canary
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
  strategy:
    canary:
      steps:
      - setWeight: 10
      - pause: { duration: 1m }
      - setWeight: 50
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you validate rollback correctness under node failure using chaos testing?
- What metrics and alerting would you use to enforce the 0-downtime guarantee?

apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1

    match:
      resources:
        kinds: ["CNFDeployment"]
    validate:

      pattern:
        metadata.attestationSigned: true
